title: Ugh fine, let’s talk about Nick Jonas in The Last Five Years one more...
transcript: As a lot of you probably know, I was very critical of the Nick Jonas casting ever since it was announced. And that is not because of any perceived lack of talent on his part. It is simply because he is not a Jewish actor. And I personally believe that the role of Jamie should really only be played by Jewish actors. But I did go into this production with an open mind, hoping that maybe he could prove me wrong. After all, we have seen non Jews do this role justice. Specifically Norbert Leo Butz, who originated the role off Broadway. But I am sad to say, upon seeing this production, a lot of my worst fears were in fact confirmed. And there's two songs in particular that I think this really becomes problematic. The first is Shiksah Goddess, which is Jamie's first song in the show. And the entire premise of that song is that he will basically date any woman as long as she's not Jewish. And obviously, that is a sentiment that coming from a Jewish man is going to read differently than coming from a non Jewish man. And he has to sing lines like, my people have suffered for thousands of years, and let me be your Hebrew slave, which, by the way, has a very different connotation when being sung to a black woman. And honestly, if it was just this song, I think I maybe would have been able to look past It. But where it gets really bad is in the song, The Schmule Song. In this song, Nick has to portray a very stereotypically Jewish Yiddish older man, down to an accent and mannerisms that feel very characterish. And in this production in particular, it kind of comes across as a joke. Like, look at this voice and these mannerisms that are typically associated with Jewish men. Aren't they so funny? Like, at one point, Nick does a very Jewish dance where he's kind of kicking his legs, and the audience laughs like it is played as a joke. Look, I don't know if the audience is laughing because, ha ha, Jewish man, funny, or just because when Nick Jonas does it, it obviously comes across as very inauthentic. But either way, I think it's problematic. And as a Jew sitting in that audience, it felt like the audience was laughing at the character because he was displaying Jewishness. While I did honestly like some aspects of Nick's performance, of those moments in particular, really soured it for me. And I wanna make two things really clear. Number one, I do not solely blame Nick Jonas in the situation. I do feel like in a lot of ways, he was set up to fail from the get go from the creative and producing teams. And number two, I am actually a Nick Jonas fan. I have seen the Jonas Brothers in concert. I even have a Jonas Brothers poster on My wall that you can see in some of my videos. This is not just me being a Nick Jonas hater and hating on him because I don't like him. I think it's important to be able to criticize things and people that you are a fan of. And I think in this instance, he and everyone else working on this production really missed the Mark here.
classificationReason: Creator explicitly attended the production ('upon seeing this production') and delivers detailed first-hand criticism of Nick Jonas's performance in specific songs. Despite the 'one more time' follow-up framing in the title, the substance is a genuine first-hand review.
